<div class="extension-guides-container">
  
  
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/ArrowHead.svg" alt="Arrow Head">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Arrow Head</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Represents general direction or flow in diagrams. In UML, it could indicate direction in an association or dependency.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/BezierCurveLine.svg" alt="Bezier Curve Line">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Bezier Curve Line</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Used for curved relationships, which might indicate non-linear or non-direct connections. In UML, it could be used for inheritance or flow that isn&#39;t straightforward.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/FilledCircleHead.svg" alt="Filled Circle Head">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Circle Head</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Used for aggregation in UML, where one class contains another but does not own it (e.g., a library containing books).</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/FilledDiamondHead.svg" alt="Filled Diamond Head">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Diamond Head</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Used for aggregation in UML, typically an empty diamond at the container end, indicating a &#34;whole-part&#34; relationship.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/FilledSquareHead.svg" alt="Filled Square Head">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Square Head</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Represents composition in UML, a stronger relationship than aggregation, where the contained class cannot exist without the container (e.g., a house and its rooms).</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/FilledTriangleHead.svg" alt="Filled Triangle Head">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Filled Triangle Head</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Often used for inheritance in UML, where one class is a subclass of another. It indicates the &#34;is-a&#34; relationship.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/LineWithCircles.svg" alt="Line With Circles">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Line With Circles</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Often represents a weak or indirect association in UML. It can also be used for dependencies or indicating optional relationships.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/SmoothLineWithCircle.svg" alt="Smooth Line With Circle">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Smooth Line With Circle</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Represents a smooth transition or flow between elements. It could be used in scenarios where gradual change or influence is depicted.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/StraightLine.svg" alt="Straight Line">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Straight Line</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Represents a simple association or direct relationship between two entities or classes in UML.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/TreeLine.svg" alt="Tree Line">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Tree Line</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Represents hierarchical relationships, such as a parent class with child classes, or a main system branching into subsystems.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/WaveLine.svg" alt="Wave Line">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Wave Line</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Typically used to represent asynchronous signals or connections that aren&#39;t continuous. It may also denote complex relationships or uncertain flows in certain custom diagrams.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/ZigzagLine.svg" alt="Zigzag Line">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Zigzag Line</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>This is often used to represent signals with interference or noise. In system design, it can be used to indicate a disrupted or unreliable connection.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
</div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Exporting Models</h1>
          
          <p>Export existing Meshery <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Models</a> or your custom infrastructure crd imported as <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Models</a> in Meshery. The platform supports a variety of application definition formats, and you can export designs using either the Meshery CLI or the Meshery UI.</p>
<h2 id="export-models-using-meshery-cli">
	Export Models Using Meshery CLI
</h2>
<p><strong>Step 1: Install Meshery CLI</strong></p>
<p>Before you can use the Meshery CLI to export a <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Model</a>, you must first install it. You can install Meshery CLI by <a href="/v0.9/installation/#install-mesheryctl">following the instructions</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Step 2: Export the Model</strong></p>
<p>Model can be exported in 2 format and OCI or Compress file. These files contain different <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">components</a>, <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/">relationships</a> files and a model file. The files can be exported in either yaml or json by default it is exported as yaml.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model export [model-name] </div></div>
</pre>
<p>Different file type and output type can be set using flags <code>-o</code> for oci and tar and <code>-t</code> for json or yaml. A location can also be specified using the -l flag where user needs to export the model</p>
<p><strong>Example :</strong></p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model export istio-base -o oci</div></div>
</pre>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model export istio-base -o oci -t json</div></div>
</pre>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> A <code>--discard-components --discard-relationships</code> flag is present to skip <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">component</a> and <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/">relationships</a> generation in the export only the model is exported without any components and relationships.</p>
<h2 id="export-models-using-meshery-ui">
	Export Models Using Meshery UI
</h2>
<p><strong>Step 1: Access the Meshery UI</strong></p>
<p>To Export a model into Meshery using the Meshery UI, you must first <a href="/v0.9/installation/quick-start/">install Meshery</a></p>
<p><strong>Step 2: Navigate to Registry under Settings Page</strong></p>
<p>Once you have accessed the Meshery UI, navigate to the Registry under Settings. This page can be accessed by clicking on the Settings on the top right on setting icon and then selecting &ldquo;Registry&rdquo; and then choose model.</p>
<p><a href="./images/Registry.png"><img alt="Registry-Navigator" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/Registry.png" /></a></p>
<p><strong>Step 3: Upload the Models</strong></p>
<p>On the Registry page, you can export your model by select Model in registry page. If no specific version the latest version is downloaded and if the specific version of model is selected then on clicking the <code>Export</code> button the model is exported as an OCI.</p>
<p>This Meshery model will include components, relationships.</p>
<p><a href="./images/ExportModel.gif"><img alt="Export-Model" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/ExportModel.gif" /></a></p>
<p>Once the Meshery model has been exported, you can export your model anytime back using <code>Import</code> on UI and then visualize on , operate and observe your components that are geneated from the crd. You can also use Meshery to deploy your Meshery Model in form of a design to any of your connected kubernetes clusters. For more information, see <a href="/v0.9/installation/kubernetes/">connections</a></p>

        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Identifying Meshery Components</h1>
          
          <p>Ever wondered what the different icons and shapes in Meshery represent? Whether you&rsquo;re looking at a dashboard, a settings page, or a design, you&rsquo;ll encounter a rich library of visual elements. This guide is here to help you understand what they mean.</p>
<p>The <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">components</a> in Meshery fall into two fundamental categories, distinguished by whether they can be orchestrated (managed) by Meshery during deployment:</p>
<ul>
<li>
<p><strong>Semantic Components (Orchestratable):</strong> These represent actual infrastructure resources that Meshery can understand and manage during deployment. Examples include Kubernetes resources (like Pods and Services), databases, and other infrastructure components. Meshery will actively manage their lifecycle during deployment.</p>
</li>
<li>
<p><strong>Non-semantic Components (Annotation):</strong> These are visual elements used for documentation and organization, such as text boxes, arrows, shapes, and comments. Meshery ignores these during deployment as they don&rsquo;t represent actual infrastructure.</p>
</li>
</ul>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Visual Customization</div>
<p>All components, whether semantic or non-semantic, support rich visual customization. For example, you can change the color of a Kubernetes Pod icon, modify its shape, or customize its background - it&rsquo;s all configurable!</p>
</div>
<h2 id="semantic-components">
	Semantic Components
</h2>
<p>These components represent real infrastructure that Meshery can manage. They can be either built-in (like Kubernetes components) or custom components that you <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-models/">create</a>.</p>
<h3 id="kubernetes-components">
	Kubernetes Components
</h3>
<p>While Kubernetes components are commonly used, they follow the same principles as all other semantic components. They have a default distinct visual style to help you instantly recognize them:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Uniform Color Scheme:</strong> Kubernetes component icons typically use a <strong>distinctive blue background</strong> as a standard identifier.</li>
<li><strong>Standardized Icon Structure:</strong> The fundamental structure is consistent: an outer container shape with the blue background, encompassing a unique inner white symbol.</li>
<li><strong>Meaningful Inner Symbols:</strong> The white symbol inside each icon is the crucial unique identifier for that specific Kubernetes Kind, often inspired by the core function of the resource.</li>
</ul>
<a href="./images/k8s_component.gif" target="_blank">
  <img src="./images/k8s_component.gif" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="Kubernetes components in Meshery">
</a>
<h3 id="integrated-technologies">
	Integrated Technologies
</h3>
<p>Meshery supports various technologies (like AWS, Prometheus, Istio, KEDA, etc.) with their official icons. These components have the same orchestratable capabilities as Kubernetes components.</p>
<a href="./images/AWS-models.png" target="_blank">
  <img src="./images/AWS-models.png" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="AWS models in Meshery">
</a>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Exploring All Integrations</div>
<p>This guide covers the visual style of components. For a complete catalog of all technologies that Meshery integrates, visit the integrations directory. <strong><a href='/extensions/integrations'>Explore All Integrations</a></strong></p>
</div>
<h2 id="non-semantic-components">
	Non-semantic Components
</h2>
<p>These components help you document and organize your designs without affecting the actual infrastructure. They include:</p>
<ul>
<li>Text boxes and comments for documentation</li>
<li>Shapes and containers for visual grouping</li>
<li>Lines and arrows for showing relationships</li>
<li>Labels and tags for organization</li>
</ul>
<p>While these components are ignored during deployment, they support the same visual customization options as semantic components.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Edge Components</div>
<p>To learn more about edge components and their visual styles, visit the <strong><a href='/extensions/edges-shape-guide'>Edge Components Guide</a></strong></p>
</div>
<h2 id="foundational-elements">
	Foundational Elements
</h2>
<p>In addition to the rich library of predefined icons, Meshery also provides a core set of foundational geometric shapes. These are not tied to any specific technology but are intended for representing abstract concepts or for simple annotations within your designs where a specific component icon doesn&rsquo;t apply.</p>
<a href="./images/shapes.png" target="_blank">
  <img src="./images/shapes.png" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="Generic shapes palette in Meshery">
</a>
<details>
<summary><strong>Foundational Geometric Shapes</strong></summary>
<br>
These are the quintessential building blocks for many diagrams – your circles, squares, triangles, and basic polygons. They offer simple, clean, and universally understood forms for a wide range of uses.

      </div>

    </div>

      </div>

    </div>

        <div style="text-align:center;">Pentagon</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A five-sided polygon often used for specific classifications of data. Its unique shape helps to quickly distinguish it from other polygonal shapes.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RoundRectangle.svg" alt="Round Rectangle">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Round Rectangle</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>Similar to a rectangle but with rounded corners, providing a softer, more approachable look. This shape is often used to visually distinguish nodes from standard rectangular nodes, indicating a special status or different type of data.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RoundTriangle.svg" alt="Round Triangle">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Round Triangle</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A triangular shape with rounded corners, providing a softer look while still indicating hierarchy or direction.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
</div>

</details>
<details>
<summary><strong>Common Representational & Symbolic Shapes</strong></summary>
<br>
This group includes shapes that, by common convention, often evoke a more specific symbolic meaning, like using a "Barrel" for data storage or an "Actor" for a user role. Leveraging these established visual metaphors can make your custom diagrams more intuitive.

      </div>

      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A six-sided shape with one or more inward curves, creating a star-like appearance, useful for special types of nodes that need to stand out distinctly.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Crescent.svg" alt="Crescent">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Crescent</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A shape resembling a crescent moon, which can be used to represent phases, growth, or transition nodes within a graph.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/CutRectangle.svg" alt="Cut Rectangle">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Cut Rectangle</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A rectangle with corners that are cut off or beveled. This shape gives a more modern and distinct appearance, often used to highlight important nodes or different types of data.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Diamond.svg" alt="Diamond">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Diamond</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A four-sided shape oriented at 45 degrees, resembling a diamond. It is typically used for decision points in flowcharts or to represent special conditions or states.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/LeftTriangle.svg" alt="Left Triangle">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Left Triangle</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A triangular shape pointing to the left, often used to indicate directional flow or hierarchical steps in processes or data sequences.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Octagon.svg" alt="Octagon">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Octagon</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>An eight-sided polygon, providing another option for representing complex data types. The additional sides make it stand out more compared to hexagons or pentagons.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Parallelogram.svg" alt="Parallelogram">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Parallelogram</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A four-sided shape with opposite sides parallel, used to represent data processing steps or functions with directional flow.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Rhomboid.svg" alt="Rhomboid">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Rhomboid</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A quadrilateral with opposite sides parallel but not perpendicular, creating a skewed rectangle look. Useful for depicting relationships that aren&#39;t straightforward or direct.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RightRhomboid.svg" alt="Right Rhomboid">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Right Rhomboid</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A rhomboid where one angle is a right angle, offering a distinctive look for special types of data connections or relationships.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RoundDiamond.svg" alt="Round Diamond">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Round Diamond</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A diamond shape with rounded corners, used to indicate special conditions or decision points while maintaining a softer visual appeal.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RoundHeptagon.svg" alt="Round Heptagon">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Round Heptagon</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A seven-sided polygon with rounded corners, less common but useful for unique data representations that require distinction.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RoundHexagon.svg" alt="Round Hexagon">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Round Hexagon</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A six-sided polygon with rounded corners, providing a less angular look for complex data types.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/RoundOctagon.svg" alt="Round Octagon">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Round Octagon</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>An eight-sided polygon with rounded corners, offering another distinct and less angular representation for complex data.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/SlantedParallelogram.svg" alt="Slanted Parallelogram">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Slanted Parallelogram</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A four-sided shape with opposite sides parallel but slanted, creating a dynamic appearance often used to indicate processes or flows that have a directional aspect.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Star.svg" alt="Star">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Star</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A shape with multiple points radiating outwards, typically used for highlighting special or notable nodes. It draws immediate attention, making it ideal for critical data points or focal nodes.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Trapezoid.svg" alt="Trapezoid">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Trapezoid</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A four-sided shape with one pair of parallel sides, used to indicate hierarchical relationships or steps in a process.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Vee.svg" alt="Vee">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Vee</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A shape resembling the letter &#34;V&#34;, often used to show directionality or a splitting point in flowcharts.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/XWing.svg" alt="XWing">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">XWing</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>This shape resembles the Star Wars X-Wing fighter, potentially useful for visually representing nodes that have multiple connections or interactions, symbolizing complexity and centrality.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Polygon.svg" alt="Polygon">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Polygon</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A custom point polygon allows the creation of irregular, user-defined polygonal shapes for graph nodes.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
    <div class="extension-guide-card">
      <div class="extension-guide-svg-container">
        
          <img src="/images/shapes/Plus.svg" alt="Plus(Polygon)">
        
        <div style="text-align:center;">Plus(Polygon)</div>
      </div>
      <div class="extension-guide-details">
        
          <div>A polygonal shape with any number of points, allowing for highly customizable node representations to fit specific data needs.</div>
        
      </div>
    </div>
  
</div>

</details>
<h2 id="component-visuals-in-different-contexts">
	Component Visuals in Different Contexts
</h2>
<p>To see how this works in practice, let&rsquo;s take the Kubernetes <code>Deployment</code> component as an example. Its appearance adapts to different views in the Meshery UI:</p>
<p>1.The full component shape as it appears in a design:</p>
<a href="./images/deployment-shape.png">
    <img src="./images/deployment-shape.png" style="width:30%; height:auto;" alt="Deployment Component Shape">
</a>
<p>2.The simplified icon as it appears in a component selection panel:</p>
<a href="./images/deployment-icon.png">
    <img src="./images/deployment-icon.png" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="Deployment icon in a component selection panel">
</a>
<p>3.The icon as seen in a cluster resource overview:</p>
<a href="./images/deployment-dashboard.png">
    <img src="./images/deployment-dashboard.png" style="width:50%; height:auto;" alt="Deployment component in a cluster resource overview">
</a>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Importing Models</h1>
          
          <p>Import your existing Models and existing custom resource definition (CRD) into Meshery. The platform supports a variety of application definition formats, and you can import designs using either the Meshery CLI or the Meshery UI.</p>
<p><strong>Note:</strong> A <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Model</a> can be only imported if it contains atleast a valid <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/">Component</a> or <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/">Relationship</a>.</p>
<h2 id="import-models-using-meshery-cli">
	Import Models Using Meshery CLI
</h2>
<div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Limitation on Importing Connections</div>
<p>The <code>mesheryctl model import</code> command currently supports importing Models containing Components, Relationships, and Policies. Importing Models with <code>Connection</code> definitions is not yet supported. This functionality may be added in a future release.</p>
</div>
<p><strong>Step 1: Install Meshery CLI</strong></p>
<p>Before you can use the Meshery CLI to import a <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/">Model</a>, you must first install it. You can install Meshery CLI by <a href="/v0.9/installation/#install-mesheryctl">following the instructions</a>.</p>
<p><strong>Step 2: Import the Model</strong></p>
<p>Model can imported in 2 different format <code>URL, File</code>.The only cretiria for this import is the model should be a Meshery exported Model.</p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model import -f [file/url] </div></div>
</pre>
<p>The supported registrant are <code>github</code>,<code>meshery</code> and <code>artifacthub</code>.The URL format must be in this order.</p>
<p><a href="https://github.com/%7Bowner%7D/%7Brepo%7D/raw/refs/heads/main/filename">https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/raw/refs/heads/main/filename</a></p>
<p><strong>Example :</strong></p>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model import -f istio-base.tar</div></div>
</pre>
<pre class="codeblock-pre">
<div class="codeblock"><div class="clipboardjs">mesheryctl model import -f "https://github.com/{owner}/{repo}/raw/refs/heads/main/filename"</div></div>
</pre>
<h2 id="import-models-using-meshery-ui">
	Import Models Using Meshery UI
</h2>
<p><strong>Step 1: Access the Meshery UI</strong></p>
<p>To import a model into Meshery using the Meshery UI, you must first <a href="/v0.9/installation/quick-start/">install Meshery</a></p>
<p><strong>Step 2: Navigate to Registry under Settings Page</strong></p>
<p>Once you have accessed the Meshery UI, navigate to the Registry under Settings. This page can be accessed by clicking on the Settings on the top right on setting icon and then selecting &ldquo;Registry&rdquo; and then choose model.</p>
<p><a href="./images/Registry.png"><img alt="Registry-Navigator" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/Registry.png" /></a></p>
<p><strong>Step 3: Upload the Model</strong></p>
<p>On the Registry page, you can import your model clicking the import button in registry page. Selecting URL or File and then hitting Import</p>
<p>This Meshery model will include components, relationships.</p>
<p><a href="./images/ImportModel.gif"><img alt="Import-Model" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/ImportModel.gif" /></a></p>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Configuration Management Guides</h1>
          
          
<p>Guides for understanding Meshery&rsquo;s ability to configure infrastructure and applications.</p>



<ul class="section-title">

  

  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/pattern-management/">Cloud Native Design Patterns</a>

        
          - Meshery applies DRY principle when managing the configuration of cloud native infrastructure.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/working-with-designs/">Configuring your Cloud Native Infrastructure and Applications</a>

        
          - Learn how to use Meshery Designs effectively
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-models/">Create Models</a>

        
          - A comprehensive guide on creating models in Meshery, covering both CLI and UI methods.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-a-meshery-design/">Creating a Meshery Design</a>

        
          - Learn how to create a Meshery design from scratch or from a template.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/edges-guide/">Edge Styles Guide</a>

        
          - Learn about the different edge styles and how to interpret their visual meaning in Meshery&#39;s component relationships.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/exporting-models/">Exporting Models</a>

        
          - Exporting Meshery Model as an OCI or Compress file
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/identifying-components/">Identifying Meshery Components</a>

        
          - A guide to help you identify and understand the various component icons, shapes, and visual styles used across the Meshery UI.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/importing-models/">Importing Models</a>

        
          - Importing Existing Model and CRD-based Infrastructure Configurations into Meshery as Model
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/push-pull-model-image/">Push or Pull a Model Image</a>

        
          - Push or pull a model image to or from an OCI-compatible image repository.
        
      </li>
    
  

</ul>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

    <language>en</language>
    <atom:link href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/index.xml" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml" />
    <item>
      <title>Cloud Native Design Patterns</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/pattern-management/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/pattern-management/</guid>
      <description>&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-warning&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;What are Cloud Native Patterns?&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This feature area is under active development. Patterns will be importable and exportable as OCI images in v0.8.0.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Patterns are essentially atomic designs with one or more components made in composed into an atomic, reusable design. Patterns are a way to apply the DRY principle when managing the configuration of cloud native infrastructure.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;use-meshery-to-deploy-a-cloud-native-pattern&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Use Meshery to Deploy a Cloud Native Pattern&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Use Meshery to deploy a cloud native pattern. Cloud native patterns are detailed as a YAML file. See the &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/&#34;&gt;Configuration Management&lt;/a&gt; guide.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Configuring your Cloud Native Infrastructure and Applications</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/working-with-designs/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/working-with-designs/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;As an cloud native management platform, Meshery has built-in support infastructure and application configuration management. Use Meshery to configure your multi-cluster Kubernetes environments on-premises or across clouds.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;what-is-a-meshery-design&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;What is a Meshery Design?&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery&amp;rsquo;s core construct of configuration management is that of a design. A design is ultimately a document – and a document in which you capture and describe your desired state of improv the environment.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/working-with-designs/images/context-aware-design.svg&#34;&gt;&lt;img class=&#34;content-image&#34; src=&#34;./images/context-aware-design.svg&#34; alt=&#34;Context Aware Design&#34;  /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Create Models</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-models/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-models/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery offers two primary ways to bring models into your system: &lt;strong&gt;Create&lt;/strong&gt; and &lt;strong&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/importing-models/&#34;&gt;Import&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/strong&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Import&lt;/strong&gt; is ideal when you already have a model definition file (e.g., JSON, CSV) and simply want to bring it into Meshery.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Create&lt;/strong&gt; is the recommended approach if you’re starting fresh — it guides you through building a model step by step using an intuitive UI wizard.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This section walks you through the &lt;strong&gt;Create&lt;/strong&gt; workflow — perfect for users who want full control over naming, styling, and categorizing their models while sourcing CRDs from GitHub or ArtifactHub.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Creating a Meshery Design</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-a-meshery-design/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/creating-a-meshery-design/</guid>
      <description>&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Learn about Designs&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Learn more about &lt;a href=&#39;/v0.9/concepts/logical/designs&#39;&gt;what a Meshery Design&lt;/a&gt; is and how it fits into Meshery&amp;rsquo;s approach to cloud native management.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;ways-to-create-a-meshery-design&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Ways to create a Meshery Design&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;You can create a Meshery design in two ways:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;from-scratch&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;From scratch&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Click on the &amp;ldquo;Design&amp;rdquo; tab to start creating a new design.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;In the left panel, click &amp;ldquo;Components&amp;rdquo; and browse the type of component you want to add.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Drag and drop the components onto the canvas.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Click and drag from one component to another to create connections between components. You can customize the connections by adding labels or adjusting their properties.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Once you&amp;rsquo;re satisfied with your design, click the &amp;ldquo;Save&amp;rdquo; button on the toolbar. Your design will be saved as &amp;ldquo;Untitled design&amp;rdquo; by default. You can give your design a name to help identify and manage it later.&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ol&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;from-a-template&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;From a template&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Another way to create a Meshery design is to use an already curated template. You can either import designs that others have published and made available for public use or clone patterns from the Meshery Catalog.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Edge Styles Guide</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/edges-guide/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/edges-guide/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;In Meshery, the line that connects &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/&#34;&gt;components&lt;/a&gt; is called an &lt;strong&gt;edge&lt;/strong&gt;. Each edge visually represents a &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/&#34;&gt;relationship&lt;/a&gt; and uses a specific style to communicate its nature.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;This guide helps you interpret the most common edge styles you will encounter.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;interpreting-common-edge-styles&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Interpreting Common Edge Styles&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery uses a set of default visual styles to provide at-a-glance information about the type of connection an edge represents. While these styles can be customized in the UI, understanding the defaults is key to interpreting component relationships.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Exporting Models</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/exporting-models/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/exporting-models/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Export existing Meshery &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/&#34;&gt;Models&lt;/a&gt; or your custom infrastructure crd imported as &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/&#34;&gt;Models&lt;/a&gt; in Meshery. The platform supports a variety of application definition formats, and you can export designs using either the Meshery CLI or the Meshery UI.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;export-models-using-meshery-cli&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Export Models Using Meshery CLI&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Step 1: Install Meshery CLI&lt;/strong&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Before you can use the Meshery CLI to export a &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/&#34;&gt;Model&lt;/a&gt;, you must first install it. You can install Meshery CLI by &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/installation/#install-mesheryctl&#34;&gt;following the instructions&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Identifying Meshery Components</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/identifying-components/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/identifying-components/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Ever wondered what the different icons and shapes in Meshery represent? Whether you&amp;rsquo;re looking at a dashboard, a settings page, or a design, you&amp;rsquo;ll encounter a rich library of visual elements. This guide is here to help you understand what they mean.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/&#34;&gt;components&lt;/a&gt; in Meshery fall into two fundamental categories, distinguished by whether they can be orchestrated (managed) by Meshery during deployment:&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Semantic Components (Orchestratable):&lt;/strong&gt; These represent actual infrastructure resources that Meshery can understand and manage during deployment. Examples include Kubernetes resources (like Pods and Services), databases, and other infrastructure components. Meshery will actively manage their lifecycle during deployment.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Importing Models</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/importing-models/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/importing-models/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Import your existing Models and existing custom resource definition (CRD) into Meshery. The platform supports a variety of application definition formats, and you can import designs using either the Meshery CLI or the Meshery UI.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;strong&gt;Note:&lt;/strong&gt; A &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/models/&#34;&gt;Model&lt;/a&gt; can be only imported if it contains atleast a valid &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/components/&#34;&gt;Component&lt;/a&gt; or &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/relationships/&#34;&gt;Relationship&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;import-models-using-meshery-cli&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Import Models Using Meshery CLI&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-warning&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;Limitation on Importing Connections&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The &lt;code&gt;mesheryctl model import&lt;/code&gt; command currently supports importing Models containing Components, Relationships, and Policies. Importing Models with &lt;code&gt;Connection&lt;/code&gt; definitions is not yet supported. This functionality may be added in a future release.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Push or Pull a Model Image</title>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Cloud Native Design Patterns</h1>
          
          <div class="alert alert-warning" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">What are Cloud Native Patterns?</div>
<p>This feature area is under active development. Patterns will be importable and exportable as OCI images in v0.8.0.</p>
</div>
<p>Patterns are essentially atomic designs with one or more components made in composed into an atomic, reusable design. Patterns are a way to apply the DRY principle when managing the configuration of cloud native infrastructure.</p>
<h2 id="use-meshery-to-deploy-a-cloud-native-pattern">
	Use Meshery to Deploy a Cloud Native Pattern
</h2>
<p>Use Meshery to deploy a cloud native pattern. Cloud native patterns are detailed as a YAML file. See the <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/">Configuration Management</a> guide.</p>
<h3 id="pattern-repository">
	Pattern Repository
</h3>
<p><em>See <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">Meshery Catalog</a></em>.</p>
<p>You may bring your own patterns or find them available through your chosen provider. Each cloud native pattern carries a unique identifier for reference. The patterns in this repository serve in an educational capacity, facilitating learning, and also serve in an operational capacity, facilitating implementation and validation of your cloud native deployment’s adherence to a pattern.</p>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Repository of Cloud Native Patterns</div>
<p>A central set of design patterns is available in Meshery Catalog (<a href='/concepts/catalog'>concept</a>, <a href='https://meshery.io/catalog'>site</a>).</p>
</div>
<h2 id="importing-patterns">
	Importing Patterns
</h2>
<p>You can import a pattern using <code>mesheryctl</code> or Meshery UI. Patterns can be imported from your local filesystem, an HTTP/S endpoint, or from GitHub. When provided a GitHub location (org/repo), Meshery will recursively search the given directory (or the entire repository) for existing pattern files.</p>
<h3 id="using-meshery-cli">
	Using Meshery CLI
</h3>
<h4 id="to-import-a-pattern-execute-this-command">
	To import a pattern, execute this command:
</h4>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>$ mesheryctl design import -f &lt;path to the pattern&gt;
Importing pattern…
Pattern imported.
</code></pre><h3 id="using-meshery-ui">
	Using Meshery UI:
</h3>
<p>From Meshery UI, patterns can be imported from your local filesystem or imported from a remote URL.</p>
<a href="./images/ImportPatternUI.png">
    <img src="./images/ImportPatternUI.png" style="width: 60%" />
</a>
<p><em>To upload from url click the link icon</em></p>
<a href="./images/UrlImport.png">
    <img src="./images/UrlImport.png" style="width: 60%" />
</a>
<h4 id="to-deploy-a-pattern-execute-this-command">
	To deploy a pattern, execute this command:
</h4>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>$ mesheryctl design apply -f &lt;path to the pattern&gt;
Deploying pattern…
Pattern successfully applied.
</code></pre><p>From here, output and behavior will vary based upon the specific pattern you’re deploying. Should you find that your pattern is not successfully deployed, refer to the pattern troubleshooting guide in the Meshery documentation.</p>
<p>As you step through each pattern, you might choose to modify the pattern to suit your specific environment and workload, exploring in-context of your specific situation. Optionally, you may choose to use a plugin like , or another visual cloud native topology tool, to facilitate your comprehension of the patterns and to literally see the patterns in-action.</p>
<p>Take time to explore. Try deploying one cloud native’s sample application onto a different cloud native and compare differences in behavior and each cloud native’s ability to manage it. If using Meshery to do so, execute the following commands as an example to deploy the sample application, BookCatalog, onto Open cloud native:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>$ mesheryctl design apply -f book-catalog
Deploying application “BookCatalog”...
Deployed. Endpoint(s) available at: http://localhost:8000/catalog
</code></pre><h2 id="related-reading">
	Related Reading
</h2>
<ul>
<li><a href="/v0.9/reference/mesheryctl/design/"><code>mesheryctl design</code></a></li>
</ul>

        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Configuring your Cloud Native Infrastructure and Applications</h1>
          
          <p>As an cloud native management platform, Meshery has built-in support infastructure and application configuration management. Use Meshery to configure your multi-cluster Kubernetes environments on-premises or across clouds.</p>
<h2 id="what-is-a-meshery-design">
	What is a Meshery Design?
</h2>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s core construct of configuration management is that of a design. A design is ultimately a document – and a document in which you capture and describe your desired state of improv the environment.</p>
<p><a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/working-with-designs/images/context-aware-design.svg"><img class="content-image" src="./images/context-aware-design.svg" alt="Context Aware Design"  /></a></p>
<h2 id="creating-a-meshery-design">
	Creating a Meshery Design
</h2>
<p>You have your choice of how are you would like to create an infrastructure design. You can use the design configurator inside of measure, UI or extensions, like , or you can hand code your design, using the mesh model spec, if you like.</p>
<p>You are free to choose how you would like to create an infrastructure design. You can use the design configurator inside of measure, UI or extensions, like , or you can hand code your design, using the mesh model spec, if you like.</p>
<p>Use Meshery UI or mesheryctl to create designs.</p>
<h2 id="pattern-management-through-meshery-ui">
	Pattern Management Through Meshery UI
</h2>
<p>Meshery also comes with seed patterns when users start Meshery for the first time. These patterns cover common use cases and examples for you as you explore Meshery.</p>
<img src="./images/meshery-patterns.png" width="50%" />
<p>Users can also import these patterns to their remote provider from this <a href="https://github.com/service-mesh-patterns/service-mesh-patterns/tree/master/samples">sample repository</a>.</p>
<img src="./images/pattern-import.png" width="50%" />
<p>Once these patterns are imported, you can then edit these patterns or use the pattern configurator to configure them according to your requirements.</p>
<img src="./images/pattern-configure-button.png" width="50%" />
<img src="./images/pattern-configure.png" width="50%" />
<h2 id="pattern-management-through-meshery-cli">
	Pattern Management Through Meshery CLI
</h2>
<p>You can also manage cloud native patterns through Meshery&rsquo;s CLI, mesheryctl.</p>
<p>The <code>mesheryctl design</code> subcommand lets you import and apply patterns to your cluster.</p>
<p>For example, if you have your pattern written in a file say, <code>istio-bookinfo.yaml</code> which deploys Istio service mesh and onboards the BookInfo app on Istio, you can use mesheryctl to apply this pattern as shown below:</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>mesheryctl design apply -f istio-bookinfo.yaml
</code></pre><p>If you already have a pattern imported into Meshery, you can apply the pattern by name.</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>mesheryctl design apply BookInfoApp
</code></pre><p>This will apply the pattern BookInfoApp, which has already been imported into Meshery.</p>
<p>See <a href="/v0.9/reference/mesheryctl/#cloud-native-pattern-configuration-and-management">mesheryctl design subcommand section</a> for more details on the <code>design</code> subcommand.</p>
<h2 id="wasm-filters">
	WASM Filters
</h2>
<p>Meshery can be used for managing WebAssembly Filters through the UI or the CLI.</p>
<h3 id="filter-management-through-meshery-ui">
	Filter Management Through Meshery UI
</h3>
<p>Like patterns, Meshery also comes with some sample WebAssembly Filters for you to experiment.</p>
<img src="./images/meshery-filters.png" width="50%" />
<p>You can also import these filters manually to your provider from the <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/wasm-filters">wasm-filters</a> repo.</p>
<p>Meshery&rsquo;s sample application <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/">ImageHub</a> will let you test out configuring these filters out-of-the-box.</p>
<p>You can onboard ImageHub to an installed service mesh as shown below.</p>
<img src="./images/image-hub.png" width="50%" />
<h3 id="filter-management-through-meshery-cli">
	Filter Management Through Meshery CLI
</h3>
<p>You can also manage WASM filters through Meshery&rsquo;s CLI, mesheryctl.</p>
<p>The <code>mesheryctl filter</code> command lets you import and configure WebAssembly filters.</p>
<p>For example,</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>mesheryctl exp filter apply -f metrics_collector_bg.wasm
</code></pre><p>If you already have a filter imported into Meshery, you can configure the filter by name.</p>
<pre tabindex="0"><code>mesheryctl exp filter apply metrics_collector_bg
</code></pre>
        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

            <h1>Guides</h1>
          
          
<p>Guides to using, operating, and troubleshooting Meshery&rsquo;s various features and components.</p>



<ul class="section-title">

  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/configuration-management/">Configuration Management Guides</a>

        
          - Guides for understanding Meshery&#39;s ability to configure infrastructure and applications
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/">Infrastructure Management Guides</a>

        
          - Guides for understanding Meshery&#39;s ability to manage infrastructure.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/mesheryctl/">Meshery CLI Guides</a>

        
          - Guides for common tasks while using Meshery&#39;s CLI, mesheryctl.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/performance-management/">Performance Management Guides</a>

        
          - Guides for understanding Meshery&#39;s ability to characterize and analyze performance of your infrastructure and applications.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/troubleshooting/">Troubleshooting Guide</a>

        
          - The documentation in the Troubleshooting section provides comprehensive guidance on troubleshooting in Meshery and its components, ensuring you can address common issues efficiently.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">

      </li>
    
  

  

</ul>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
