        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Envoy WASM Filter Management</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery offers powerful features that simplify the management of Envoy WASM filters in Istio.</p>
<h3 id="meshery-ui-and-cli-integration">
	Meshery UI and CLI Integration
</h3>
<ul>
<li><strong>Import WASM Envoy Filters</strong>: Easily import your WebAssembly Envoy filters into Meshery using the intuitive UI or the command-line interface (<a href="https://docs.meshery.io/reference/mesheryctl#data-plane-intelligence">CLI</a>).</li>
<li><strong>Publish and Clone Filters</strong>: Share your filters with the community by publishing them in the <a href="https://meshery.io/catalog">Meshery Catalog</a> and make it effortless for others to clone them.</li>
<li><strong>Download WASM Binaries</strong>: Access and download WebAssembly binaries directly from your Remote Provider like <a href="https://cloud.meshery.io/">Meshery Cloud</a>.</li>
<li><strong>Contribute to Open Source</strong>: Get involved with the cloud native community by contributing to any of the open source <a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/wasm-filters">wasm-filters</a> developed by the Meshery community.</li>
</ul>
<img src="https://mcusercontent.com/6b50be5aea3dfe1fd4c041d80/images/a07ef29a-4cf8-986e-9bd3-78db7dc00ce1.png" width="100px" style="float:left;position:relative;margin: 1rem 1rem 1rem 0rem" />
<h2 id="envoy-wasm-filter-management">
	Envoy WASM Filter Management
</h2>
<p>As of Meshery v0.7, the management of Envoy WASM filters includes:</p>
<p><strong>Meshery Server Integration</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ New WASM Filter Component: A new component is available in the Design Configurator to simplify filter management.</li>
<li>✅ Improved Component Icon: Enhancements have been made to provide a more user-friendly experience.</li>
<li>✅ Relationship Patch Policy: A new policy has been introduced to streamline the relationship between components.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Import Filters: Use <code>mesheryctl filter import [URL | filepath]</code> to effortlessly import filters.</li>
<li>✅ Delete Filters: Remove unwanted filters with <code>mesheryctl filter delete [filter-name | ID]</code>.</li>
<li>✅ View Filters: Gain insights into your filters using <code>mesheryctl filter view [filter-name | ID]</code>.</li>
<li>✅ List and Search Filters: Easily navigate filters with <code>mesheryctl filter list [filter-name | ID]</code>.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong> Integration</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Apply WASM Filters: Hierarchically apply filters to your Envoy configurations.</li>
<li>✅ Deploy/Undeploy Filters: Streamline the deployment and removal of filters with custom configurations.</li>
<li>✅ Enhanced Visibility: View filters within a dedicated panel and seamlessly drop them onto the canvas.</li>
</ul>
<img src="https://mcusercontent.com/6b50be5aea3dfe1fd4c041d80/images/1e9c2e71-1b3e-a132-4766-8cefdc9861d2.png" width="50px" style="float:left;position:relative;margin: 1rem 1rem 1rem 0rem" />
<p><strong>Meshery UI Enhancements</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Import Filters: Import filters directly via URL or filesystem.</li>
<li>✅ Improved Browsing: Browse, search, and view filters in both grid view and table view.</li>
<li>✅ Streamlined Lists: Easily list and search filters in grid view or table view.</li>
<li>✅ Download Filters: Download filters effortlessly from the UI.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Remote Provider and Meshery Catalog Integration</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Permanent Storage and Artifact Dispersal: Ensure your filters are securely stored and widely accessible.</li>
<li>✅ Catalog Features: Import, clone, download, publish, and unpublish filters within the Meshery Catalog.</li>
<li>✅ Enhanced Privacy Controls: Manage user permissions, team ownership, and visibility for your filters.</li>
<li>✅ Content Curation: Streamline content curation with an approval flow request queue.</li>
</ul>
<h2 id="performance-management-upgrades">
	Performance Management Upgrades
</h2>
<p>In addition to Envoy WASM filter management, we&rsquo;ve also introduced new performance management features:</p>
<p><strong>Meshery Server</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Performance Profiles: Tailor your performance profiles to match your specific needs.</li>
<li>✅ SSL Certificate Support: Benefit from SSL certificate support for Fortio in the server.</li>
<li>✅ Performance Analysis Comparison: Compare performance with and without filters.</li>
<li>✅ GetNighthawk and Cloud Native Performance Releases: Access the latest releases of GetNighthawk and Cloud Native Performance.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Meshery CLI</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Performance Profile Flags: Specify additional load generator flags with performance profiles.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Meshery UI</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Performance Profile Flags: Customize load generator flags directly in the UI.</li>
</ul>
<p><strong>Service Performance Project</strong></p>
<ul>
<li>✅ Define Performance Profiles: Clearly define your performance profiles.</li>
<li>✅ Dashboard Integration: Display test results on the dashboard.</li>
<li>✅ Intel Integration: Incorporate Intel design into scheduled workflows for Istio.</li>
<li>✅ Consolidated Performance Profiles: Streamline performance profiles on the dashboard.</li>
</ul>
<p>Meshery offers WebAssembly-based network traffic management filters in Envoy, bringing a new level of flexibility and control to your Istio deployments.</p>
<h2 id="frequently-asked-questions">
	Frequently Asked Questions
</h2>
<h3 id="q-why-does-meshery-provide-and-manage-wasm-filters">
	Q: Why does Meshery provide and manage WASM filters?
</h3>
<p>Meshery manages WASM filters for data plane proxies for:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>Agility</strong>: in partnership with service mesh control planes, Meshery can dynamically load, configure, and unload filter(s) in running Envoy proxies.</li>
<li><strong>Maintainability</strong>: To extend the functionality we don’t have to change the entire codebase.</li>
<li><strong>Diversity</strong> : WASM filters can be easily compiled with many popular programming languages like C/C++ and Rust.</li>
<li><strong>Reliability and isolation</strong> : WASM filters are deployed into VM and hence they are isolated from the Envoy process. For instance if the WASM filter crashes it will not impact the envoy process.</li>
<li><strong>Security</strong> : The WASM filter uses a well defined API to connect with the host i.e envoy proxy which can be modified only a limited number of connections.</li>
<li><strong>Speed</strong> : It is originally used to speed up large web application</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="q-what-is-envoy-proxy">
	Q: What is Envoy proxy?
</h3>
<h3 id="q-what-is-wasm-">
	Q: What is WASM ?
</h3>
<p>WebAssembly is a low-level assembly-like language with a compact binary format that runs with near-native performance and provides languages such as C/C++, C# and Rust with a compilation target so that they can run in many different environments, including behind Envoy&rsquo;s Application Binary Interface to extend Envoy with new capabilities. WASM programs are distributed in an efficient portable binary instruction format and embed into isolated execution environments.</p>
<h3 id="q-what-are-the-disadvantages-of-wasm-filters-to-be-taken-into-consideration">
	Q: What are the disadvantages of WASM filters to be taken into consideration?
</h3>
<p>Execution of WASM filters requires system resources. Just as executing the same functionality that your filter provides outside of the WASM virtual machine, resources can include overhead of latency, CPU, and memory. See the <a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a> project for more detail.</p>
<h3 id="q-what-is-the-envoy-proxy-wasm-sdk">
	Q: What is the Envoy Proxy WASM SDK?
</h3>
<p>Envoy proxy runs the WASM filter in a stack-based virtual machine so that the filter memory is isolated from the host environment. The interaction between the embedded host i.e. Envoy proxy and the WASM filter are done via call backs and functions by the Envoy Proxy WASM SDK. The Envoy Proxy WASM SDK is implemented in various programming languages like C++, RUST, AssemblyScript and GO(still experimental)</p>
<h3 id="q-what-is-image-hub-">
	Q: What is Image Hub ?
</h3>
<p>Image Hub is a sample application which was first officially demonstrated at DockerCon 2020. This sample application is written to run on consul to explore the WebAssembly (WASM) modules in the Envoy filter. This application is written in the RUST programming language. These modules are used to implement the multi-tenancy or to implement the per user rate limiting in the applications endpoint.</p>

    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';

            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';

            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

            <h1>GitOps with Meshery</h1>
          
          <h2 id="-snapshot-github-action">
	<img style="height: 4rem; width: 4rem;" src="./images/-icon-color.svg" />  Snapshot GitHub Action
</h2>
<ul>
<li>See your deployment before you merge</li>
<li>Connect  to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request</li>
<li>Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs</li>
</ul>
<h3>Using Meshery's SnapShot GitHub Action</h3>
See your deployment before you merge. Connect  to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request. Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs.
<p>See <a href="/extensions/snapshot">Extension:  Snapshot</a> for more details.</p>
<h2 id="meshery-performance-analysis-github-action">
	<img src="./images/smp-dark-text-side.svg" className="image-left-no-shadow" alt="Infrastructure fperformance logo" style="width: 60%; max-width: 200px;vertical-align:middle" /> Meshery Performance Analysis GitHub Action
</h2>
<ul>
<li>See your performance regressions before you merge</li>
<li>Connect Performance Management to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request</li>
<li>Red light performance regressions</li>
<li>Baseline and analyze the performance of your services is key to efficient operation of any application
<ul>
<li>Meshery is the canonical implementation of the Cloud Native Performance specification</li>
</ul>
</li>
<li>Define your performance profiles upfront. See statistical analysis with microservice latency and throughput quartiles</li>
<li>Meshery includes your choice of load generator, so that you can meausure your way</li>
<li>Meshery packages all these features into an easy-to-use GitHub Action</li>
</ul>
<p>Measuring and managing the performance of your infrastructure is key to efficient operation. You can choose from multiple load generators and use a highly configurable set of load profiles with variable tunable facets to run a performance test. Meshery packages all these features into an easy-to-use GitHub Action.</p>
<h3>Using Meshery's Performance Analysis GitHub Action</h3>
<p>The <a href="https://github.com/marketplace/actions/performance-testing-with-meshery">Meshery Performance Analysis GitHub Action</a> is available in the GitHub Marketplace. You can create your own performance profiles to run repeatable tests with Meshery. You can configure this action to trigger with each of your releases, on every pull request or any GitHub workflow trigger event. A sample configuration of the action is shown below.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Meshery SMP Action</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">on</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">push</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">branches</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span><span class="s1">&#39;master&#39;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">jobs</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">performance-test</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Performance Test</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">runs-on</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">ubuntu-latest</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">    </span><span class="nt">steps</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span>- <span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">checkout</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">uses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">actions/checkout@v2</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">with</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">ref</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s1">&#39;perf&#39;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span>- <span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Deploy k8s-minikube</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">uses</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">manusa/actions-setup-minikube@v2.4.1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">with</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">minikube version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s1">&#39;v1.21.0&#39;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">kubernetes version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s1">&#39;v1.20.7&#39;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">driver</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">docker</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">      </span>- <span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Run Performance Test</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">        </span><span class="nt">with</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">provider_token</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">${{ secrets.PROVIDER_TOKEN }}</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">platform</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">docker</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">          </span><span class="nt">profile_name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">soak-test</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><p>You can also define your test configuration in an SMP compatible configuration file as shown below.</p>
<div class="highlight"><pre tabindex="0" class="chroma"><code class="language-yaml" data-lang="yaml"><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">smp_version</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">v0.0.1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">id</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">name</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">Istio Performance Test</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">labels</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span>{}<span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">clients</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl">- <span class="nt">internal</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="kc">false</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">load_generator</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="l">fortio</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">protocol</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">1</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">connections</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">2</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">rps</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="m">10</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">headers</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span>{}<span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">cookies</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span>{}<span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">body</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">content_type</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span><span class="nt">endpoint_urls</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="w">  </span>- <span class="l">http://localhost:2323/productpage</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span><span class="line"><span class="cl"><span class="nt">duration</span><span class="p">:</span><span class="w"> </span><span class="s2">&#34;30m&#34;</span><span class="w">
</span></span></span></code></pre></div><p>See this sample GitHub workflow (<a href="https://github.com/meshery-extensions/meshery-smp-action/blob/master/action.yml">action.yml</a>) for more configuration details.</p>
<p><a href="./images/service-mesh-performance-profile-test-results.png"><img src="./images/service-mesh-performance-profile-test-results.png" className="image-center" alt="performance management dashboard" /></a></p>
<p>The results from the tests are updated on the Performance Management dashboard in Meshery. To learn more about interpreting the test results, check out <a href="/guides/performance-management/interpreting-performance-test-results">this guide</a>. You can always checkout the <a href="/guides">Meshery User Guides</a> to dive deep into these features.</p>
<p><a href="https://smp-spec.io">Cloud Native Performance</a> standardizes infrastructure measurement, characterizing any deployment&rsquo;s performance by capturing the details of infrastructure capacity, configuration and workload metadata.</p>

            <h1>Infrastructure Management Guides</h1>
          
          
<p>Guides for understanding Meshery&rsquo;s ability to manage infrastructure.</p>



<ul class="section-title">

  

  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/">Deploying Sample Applications</a>

        
          - This guide is to help users get a better understanding of sample apps
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/filter-management/">Envoy WASM Filter Management</a>

        
          - Meshery provides the ability to manage WASM filters for data plane proxies for agility, maintainability, diversity, reliability and isolation, security, and speed.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/gitops-with-meshery/">GitOps with Meshery</a>

        
          - Integrating your CI/CD pipelines with Meshery&#39;s GitHub Actions
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/registering-a-connection/">Infrastructure Discovery</a>

        
          - MeshSync supports both greenfield and brownfield discovery of infrastructure. Greenfield discovery manages infrastructure created and managed entirely by Meshery, while brownfield discovery identifies separately created infrastructure.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/overview/">Infrastructure Management</a>

        
          - Meshery provides the ability to manage infrastructure for agility, maintainability, diversity, reliability and isolation, security, and speed.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management/">Managing Connections</a>

        
          - Manage the lifecycle of your infrastructure by registering each infrastructure element with Meshery.
        
      </li>
    
  
    
      <li style="list-style-type: disc; margin: 2px 0;">
        <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management/">Managing Events with Notification Center</a>

        
          - Meshery tracks operations performed on your infrastructure and workloads, and provides notification of environment issues, application conflicts with infrastructure configuration, policy violations, and so on.
        
      </li>
    
  

</ul>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

<?xml version="1.0" encoding="utf-8" standalone="yes"?>
<rss version="2.0" xmlns:atom="http://www.w3.org/2005/Atom">
  <channel>
    <title>Infrastructure Management Guides on Documentation</title>
    <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/</link>
    <description>Recent content in Infrastructure Management Guides on Documentation</description>
    <generator>Hugo</generator>
    <language>en</language>
    <atom:link href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/index.xml" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml" />
    <item>
      <title>Deploying Sample Applications</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery includes a few sample applications to help you explore cloud native infrastructure. Each is a collection of microservices for experimental purposes of learning about running workloads in Kubernetes clusters both on and off of cloud native infrastructure. When deploying a sample app onto your cloud native infrastructure, your sample application needs will need to be externaally exposed from the cluster, if you would like to access it externally. There are a myriad of ways to do this, specific to the infrastructure you are using.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Envoy WASM Filter Management</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/filter-management/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/filter-management/</guid>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>GitOps with Meshery</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/gitops-with-meshery/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/gitops-with-meshery/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;-snapshot-github-action&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;&lt;img style=&#34;height: 4rem; width: 4rem;&#34; src=&#34;./images/-icon-color.svg&#34; /&gt;  Snapshot GitHub Action&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;See your deployment before you merge&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Connect  to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;li&gt;Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs&lt;/li&gt;&#xA;&lt;/ul&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3&gt;Using Meshery&#39;s SnapShot GitHub Action&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;See your deployment before you merge. Connect  to your GitHub repo and see changes pull request-to-pull request. Get snapshots of your infrastructure directly in your PRs.&#xA;&lt;p&gt;See &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/extensions/snapshot&#34;&gt;Extension:  Snapshot&lt;/a&gt; for more details.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Infrastructure Discovery</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/registering-a-connection/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/registering-a-connection/</guid>
      <description>&lt;div class=&#34;alert alert-info&#34; role=&#34;alert&#34;&gt;&lt;div class=&#34;h4 alert-heading&#34; role=&#34;heading&#34;&gt;MeshSync&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Managed by the &lt;a href=&#39;/v0.9/concepts/architecture/operator&#39;&gt;Meshery Operator&lt;/a&gt;, MeshSync is a custom Kubernetes controller that provides tiered discovery and continual synchronization with Meshery Server as to the state of the Kubernetes clusters and their workloads. Learn more about &lt;a href=&#39;/v0.9/concepts/architecture/meshsync&#39;&gt;MeshSync&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;/div&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;MeshSync is your tool for efficient management and synchronization of Kubernetes clusters! This user guide will walk you through how to establish a connection with any element that Meshery is able to connect to and manage. Use the MeshSync page to register connections, view connection metadata, and perform connectivity tests, as weel as to manage credentials and environments.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Infrastructure Management</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/overview/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/overview/</guid>
      <description>&lt;h2 id=&#34;using-meshery-designs-to-manage-your-infrastructure&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Using Meshery Designs to Manage Your Infrastructure&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery is a versatile platform designed to streamline the lifecycle, configuration, and performance management of infrastructure across Kubernetes clusters.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;designs-in-meshery&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Designs in Meshery&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery employs the concept of &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/concepts/logical/designs/&#34;&gt;Designs&lt;/a&gt; as a fundamental construct for managing infrastructure. Designs provide a structured way to organize and deploy various components of your infrastructure. To do so, Meshery utilizes a declarative approach to infrastructure management, similar to Kubernetes manifests. Meshery Designs are written in YAML and are validated against a schema.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Managing Connections</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;&lt;a name=&#34;lifecycle-management&#34;&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery manages hundreds of different types of cloud native infrastructure. See the &lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/extensibility/integrations&#34;&gt;full set of integrations&lt;/a&gt;.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h2 id=&#34;cloud-native-infrastructure-lifecycle-management&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;Cloud Native Infrastructure Lifecycle Management&#xA;&lt;/h2&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;&lt;a href=&#34;/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management/images/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg&#34;&gt;&lt;img class=&#34;content-image&#34; src=&#34;./images/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg&#34; alt=&#34;Lifecycle Management&#34;  /&gt;&lt;/a&gt;&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery Adapters can optionally be deployed to provide deep support of different types of infrastructure, so that you can learn and compare different infrastructure functionality. Once you have selected to operate a given infrastructure, Meshery will assist you with ongoing operations.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;Meshery automates the provisioning of various infrastructurees, allowing users to select different configuration profiles in order to support a variety of deployment models.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
    <item>
      <title>Managing Events with Notification Center</title>
      <link>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management/</link>
      <pubDate>Mon, 01 Jan 0001 00:00:00 +0000</pubDate>
      <guid>/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management/</guid>
      <description>&lt;p&gt;Meshery continuously tracks activities affecting your infrastructure and workloads. Meshery generates a variety of events, reflecting activities affecting the design and operation of your infrastructure whether those activities are directly or indirectly performed through Meshery operations.&lt;/p&gt;&#xA;&lt;h3 id=&#34;what-is-the-notification-center&#34;&gt;&#xA;&#x9;What is the Notification Center?&#xA;&lt;/h3&gt;&#xA;&lt;p&gt;The Notification Center is a dedicated panel in Meshery’s UI that helps you monitor, understand, and respond to events across your system. It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.&lt;/p&gt;</description>
    </item>
  </channel>
</rss>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Managing Connections</h1>
          
          <p><a name="lifecycle-management"></a></p>
<p>Meshery manages hundreds of different types of cloud native infrastructure. See the <a href="/extensibility/integrations">full set of integrations</a>.</p>
<h2 id="cloud-native-infrastructure-lifecycle-management">
	Cloud Native Infrastructure Lifecycle Management
</h2>
<p><a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/lifecycle-management/images/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg"><img class="content-image" src="./images/states-for-kubernetes-cluster-connections.svg" alt="Lifecycle Management"  /></a></p>
<p>Meshery Adapters can optionally be deployed to provide deep support of different types of infrastructure, so that you can learn and compare different infrastructure functionality. Once you have selected to operate a given infrastructure, Meshery will assist you with ongoing operations.</p>
<p>Meshery automates the provisioning of various infrastructurees, allowing users to select different configuration profiles in order to support a variety of deployment models.</p>
<p>Meshery adapters will dynamically retrieve the specific infrastructure&rsquo;s release package upon initial deployment of a given infrastructure. Meshery adapters cache (in <code>.meshery/bin</code>) the infrastructure installation package.</p>
<h4 id="deprovisioning-infrastructure">
	Deprovisioning infrastructure
</h4>
<p>Just as Meshery automates the provisioning of various cloud native infrastructure, so too does it facilitate the deprovisioning of infrastructure. Find the &ldquo;Undeploy&rdquo; button in Meshery UI or the <code>--undeploy</code> flag in Meshery CLI.</p>
<h2 id="workload-lifecycle-management">
	Workload Lifecycle Management
</h2>
<p>Users may bring their applications (perform workload onboarding) on the infrastructure using the Custom Configuration operation.</p>
<p>Commonly adjoining each infrastructure is a sample application that facilitates demonstration of the value of the given infrastructure. Meshery allows you to efficiently <a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/sample-apps/">install sample applications</a> across different infrastructurees.</p>
<h2 id="configuration-management">
	Configuration Management
</h2>
<p>Meshery provides the ability for you as a infrastructure manager to customize your infrastructure deployment.</p>
<h2 id="notifications">
	Notifications
</h2>
<p>Meshery tracks operations that you perform on infrastructurees and their workloads. Meshery provides notification of environment issues, application conflicts with infrastructure configuration, and so on.</p>
<h4 id="acknowledging-and-dismissing-notifications">
	Acknowledging and dismissing notifications
</h4>
<p>Depending upon the severity of the notification, many notifications are informational and can readily be dismissed after reading. Some notifications include actionable alerts. Learn more in &ldquo;<a href="/v0.9/guides/infrastructure-management/notification-management/">Managing Events with Notification Center</a>&rdquo;.</p>
<h2 id="lifecycle-faqs">
	Lifecycle FAQs
</h2>
<details>
<summary>
<strong>Question:</strong> “Meshery is a collaboration platform. When I bring my infrastructure under Meshery's management, will my Kubernetes clusters be available to all other users? Can other people access my cluster?
</summary><strong>Answer:</strong> <p>Yes, they can, <i>IF</i> you explicitly allow them to do so. It's important to understand the following controls and system behavior:</p>
<p><b>1. Ownership:</b> Every connection to a Kubernetes cluster is created by and owned by the individual that provided the Kubernetes context. That individual may elect to share the connection with others on their team (if you have invited anyone to your team(s)).</p>
<p><b>2. Permission:</b> If you do grant other team members access, you do so by creating an environment, assigning that Kubernetes connection to the environment, then creating a workspace and assigning that environment to the workspace. Users of any of your teams to which you have shared access to the workspace will then have permission to access the cluster.</p>
<p><b>3. Connectivity:</b> those individuals will have to be afforded network connectivity to that cluster (in whatever fashion you deem appropriate). Grossly, there are two ways in which this can occur:</p>
<p>3.a) The other user runs their own copy of Meshery (or signs into a shared instance like the Playground) and will see the connection as being available when they sign in. Their Meshery Server will need to be able to reach your Kube API over the network. How that is done can be any number of ways and is left unto your own devices.</p>
<p>3.b.) The other user signs into your Meshery Server instance, which has network access to your Kubernetes cluster. In order for the other user to sign into your Meshery Server, you would have to expose it to the Internet or VPN or… one of the many other ways to all them access to your Meshery Server.</p>
<p>So, in short, yes, you can share access to your Kubernetes cluster with other users, but you have to explicitly grant them access to do so. For more information please visit <a href="/extensibility/authorization">Remote Provider Permissions</a>.</p>
</details>
<div class="alert alert-dark" role="alert">
  <h4 class="alert-heading">Discussion Forum</h4>
  <p>Don't find an answer to your question here? Ask on the <a href="https://discuss.meshery.io">Discussion Forum</a>.</p>
</div>

            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';

                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

            <h1>Managing Events with Notification Center</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery continuously tracks activities affecting your infrastructure and workloads. Meshery generates a variety of events, reflecting activities affecting the design and operation of your infrastructure whether those activities are directly or indirectly performed through Meshery operations.</p>
<h3 id="what-is-the-notification-center">
	What is the Notification Center?
</h3>
<p>The Notification Center is a dedicated panel in Meshery’s UI that helps you monitor, understand, and respond to events across your system. It acts as a central place where you can see important updates related to your infrastructure, workloads, and Meshery’s internal operations.</p>
<a href="./images/find-notification-center.gif">
  <img src="./images/find-notification-center.gif" alt="Notification Position" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a>
<h3 id="types-of-notifications">
	Types of Notifications
</h3>
<p>Given the variety of activities that occur through the process of managing infrastructure, notifications have been grouped into categories so that you can readily understand what a notification means and what do to about any particular type you have received.</p>
<p>Each notification in Meshery includes a clear summary of what occurred in your system. Notifications vary in format depending on the event type, but typically include:</p>
<ul>
<li>Action performed (e.g., saved a design, ran a dry run)</li>
<li>Affected components (e.g., deployments, MeshSync, events)</li>
<li>Validation results or errors (e.g., invalid values, missing fields)</li>
<li>Relationship updates (e.g., how components are linked)</li>
<li>Links to the related design or further details</li>
</ul>
<p>You can mark notifications as read or unread to stay organized and focused. Meshery highlights critical, actionable events in red, helping you quickly spot and respond to urgent issues.</p>
<a href="./images/description.png">
  <img src="./images/description.png" alt="Event Descriptions" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a>
<blockquote>
<p>🔗 For more technical details, see the <a href="https://docs.meshery.io/project/contributing/contributing-ui-notification-center">Contributor Reference</a>.</p>
</blockquote>
<h3 id="notification-timestamps">
	Notification Timestamps
</h3>
<p>Each notification includes a timestamp showing when the event happened. The time is displayed based on your local device’s time zone, so it reflects your current time.</p>
<a href="./images/timestamps.png">
  <img src="./images/timestamps.png" alt="Notification Timestamps" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a>
<h3 id="data-sharing">
	Data Sharing
</h3>
<p>Need to collaborate?
You can share notifications with teammates or stakeholders in just a few clicks — making it easier to communicate and resolve issues.</p>
<a href="./images/notification-share.png">
  <img src="./images/notification-share.png" alt="Notification Share" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a>
<h3 id="filtering-and-searching">
	Filtering and Searching
</h3>
<p>The Notification Center provides a powerful way to filter and search through events. You can narrow down results using filters such as <strong>severity</strong>, <strong>status</strong>, <strong>action</strong>, <strong>category</strong>, and <strong>author</strong>.</p>
<blockquote>
<p>Note: Some filter options such as <code>action</code>, <code>category</code>, and <code>author</code> are dynamically generated based on the notifications your Meshery instance has received. These values are retrieved from the <code>/api/system/events/types</code> endpoint.</p>
</blockquote>
<a href="./images/notification-filter.gif">
  <img src="./images/notification-filter.gif" alt="Notification Filter" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a>
<h4 id="severity">
	Severity
</h4>
<p>Filter notifications based on the level of severity, indicated by icon color and symbol. These levels are defined in the <code>SEVERITY</code> constant and styled using <code>SEVERITY_STYLE</code>.</p>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Level</th>
          <th>Code Value</th>
          <th>Icon</th>
          <th>Color (Light Mode)</th>
          <th>Description</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td>Info</td>
          <td><code>informational</code></td>
          <td>ℹ️ InfoIcon</td>
          <td>Blue</td>
          <td>General updates or logs</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>Warning</td>
          <td><code>warning</code></td>
          <td>⚠️ AlertIcon</td>
          <td>Yellow</td>
          <td>Potential issues</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>Error</td>
          <td><code>error</code></td>
          <td>❌ ErrorIcon</td>
          <td>Red</td>
          <td>Failures or critical problems</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>Success</td>
          <td><code>success</code></td>
          <td>✅ InfoIcon</td>
          <td>Green</td>
          <td>Successfully completed actions</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<h4 id="status">
	Status
</h4>
<p>Filter notifications based on whether they have been read. These statuses are defined in <code>STATUS</code> and styled using <code>STATUS_STYLE</code>.</p>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Status</th>
          <th>Code Value</th>
          <th>Icon</th>
          <th>Description</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td>Read</td>
          <td><code>read</code></td>
          <td>ReadIcon</td>
          <td>Notifications that have been opened</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>Unread</td>
          <td><code>unread</code></td>
          <td>EnvelopeIcon</td>
          <td>New or untouched notifications</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<h3 id="understanding-notification-logos-and-icons">
	Understanding Notification Logos and Icons
</h3>
<p>Meshery uses avatar icons to indicate who triggered a notification and what system was involved. These icons help users quickly understand the origin and nature of each event.</p>
<a href="./images/avatar-icons.png">
  <img src="./images/avatar-icons.png" alt="Avatar Icons" style="width: 600px; height: auto; margin-top: 10px;" />
</a>
<table>
  <thead>
      <tr>
          <th>Icon Type</th>
          <th>Meaning</th>
      </tr>
  </thead>
  <tbody>
      <tr>
          <td>Meshery logo only</td>
          <td>System-triggered event – initiated automatically by Meshery (e.g., syncing errors, import failures).</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>User avatar + Meshery logo</td>
          <td>User-triggered event – the user performed an action, and Meshery processed it (e.g., registering a Kubernetes context).</td>
      </tr>
      <tr>
          <td>User avatar only (rare)</td>
          <td>User-triggered event with no system action involved.</td>
      </tr>
  </tbody>
</table>
<p>These icons are generated dynamically using the event’s metadata:</p>
<ul>
<li>If <code>user_id</code> is present → shows user avatar.</li>
<li>If <code>system_id</code> is present → shows Meshery logo.</li>
</ul>
<details close><summary>Visual Representation of System/User-triggered Notifications</summary>
  <br>
  <figure>
    <figcaption>
      1. 🟢 Meshery-only (System-triggered) Notification
      <a target="_blank" href="https://playground.meshery.io/extension/meshmap?mode=design&design=a7310bb4-e642-4e4e-807a-dbb602228f07">
        (open in playground)
      </a>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div id="embedded-design-a7310bb4-e642-4e4e-807a-dbb602228f07" style="height:30rem;width:100%;"></div>
  <script src="./images/meshery-triggered.js" type="module"></script>
  <figure>
    <figcaption>
      2. 👤+🌐 User + Meshery (User-triggered) Notification
      <a target="_blank" href="https://playground.meshery.io/extension/meshmap?mode=design&design=a96a3008-9c36-4862-b1e3-20cc2c35ca89">
        (open in playground)
      </a>
    </figcaption>
  </figure>
  <div id="embedded-design-a96a3008-9c36-4862-b1e3-20cc2c35ca89" style="height:30rem;width:100%;"></div>
  <script src="./images/user-triggered.js" type="module"></script>
</details>
<h3 id="notification-retention-and-visibility">
	Notification Retention and Visibility
</h3>
<p><strong>How long are notifications stored?</strong></p>
<p>The duration for which notifications are retained is determined by the provider you are using (e.g., Meshery Cloud, local Meshery Server).</p>
<p><strong>What happens when retention ends?</strong></p>
<p>In Meshery Cloud, notifications are removed once the provider is updated, helping ensure the event stream reflects the most recent and relevant information.</p>

    $(document).ready(function () {

        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)

            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];

            })

        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {

                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });

            <h1>Infrastructure Management</h1>
          
          <h2 id="using-meshery-designs-to-manage-your-infrastructure">
	Using Meshery Designs to Manage Your Infrastructure
</h2>
<p>Meshery is a versatile platform designed to streamline the lifecycle, configuration, and performance management of infrastructure across Kubernetes clusters.</p>
<h3 id="designs-in-meshery">
	Designs in Meshery
</h3>
<p>Meshery employs the concept of <a href="/v0.9/concepts/logical/designs/">Designs</a> as a fundamental construct for managing infrastructure. Designs provide a structured way to organize and deploy various components of your infrastructure. To do so, Meshery utilizes a declarative approach to infrastructure management, similar to Kubernetes manifests. Meshery Designs are written in YAML and are validated against a schema.</p>
<h4 id="importing-existing-infrastructure-and-applications">
	Importing Existing Infrastructure and Applications
</h4>
<p>Meshery facilitates the import of infrastructure in multiple formats, including Kubernetes manifests, Helm Charts, and Docker Compose files. Import existing infrastructure definitions by directly from filesystem, via URL, or import directly from a GitHub repository.</p>
<ul>
<li>Kubernetes Manifest</li>
<li>Meshery Design</li>
<li>Helm Charts</li>
<li>Docker Compose</li>
</ul>
<p>See <a href="/v0.9/extensions/import-export-designs/">Importing Designs</a> for more information.</p>
<details>
<summary>
<h3>Meshery Internals Provisioning Process</h3>
</summary>
<p>When a request is made to provision a design, it undergoes the following stages:</p>
<h4>1. Import of Referenced Designs</h4>
<p>A Design may reference any number of other Designs, in essence, a Design may import any number of other Designs.  As an editor of a Design, you can make reference to another Design, while following principles of reusing and DRY (Do Not Repeat Yourself). Any referenced Design will subsequently be imported during the provisioning moment. To reference another design, do so by adding the following annotation <pre>type: $(#use \<url-of-remote-pattern\>)</pre> in your Design file. The referenced design will be expanded from the source.</p>
<h4>2. Identification</h4>
<p>Meshery relies on components registered at boot time. Only registered models and components can be managed with Meshery. Currently, models from the ArtifactHub repository are supported.</p>
<h4>3. Validation</h4>
<p>Components in the design are validated against the schema, ensuring consistency, similar to Kubernetes object validation but tailored for Designs.</p>
<h4>4. Dependency Detection and Resolution</h4>
<p>Meshery identifies and resolves dependencies among components using a dynamic mechanism based on each component’s origin (also known as its <code>host</code> or <code>registrant</code>). Provisioning order is critical—circular dependencies will result in termination of the deployment.</p>
<p>Deployment Mechanism by Source:</p>
<ul>
  <li><b>Artifact Hub:</b> Uses Helm Go client for Kubernetes Operator and CRD deployment via <code>ApplyHelmChart()</code>.</li>
  <li><b>Kubernetes YAML:</b> Direct application with Kubernetes Go client (no auto-dependency handling).</li>
</ul>
<p>This behavior is determined by the component’s host type:</p>
<pre>
if connection.Kind == "artifacthub" ➜ Helm Go client used
if connection.Kind == "kubernetes" ➜ Kubernetes Go client used
</pre>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Implementation Detail</div>
<p>This logic is handled in the <code>NewDependencyHandler()</code> function, which selects the deployment method based on <code>connection.Kind</code>.</p>
</div>
<h4>5. Provisioning</h4>
<p>A Directed Acyclic Graph (DAG) generated in the previous step is processed. Dependent components are processed sequentially, while others are processed in parallel. Meshery intelligently handles the deployment order to ensure successful deployment.</p>
</details>
<h3>Auto-Deployment of CRDs and Operators</h3>
<p>Meshery automates the deployment of Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) and operators based on the source from which a particular component was registered. By default, Meshery automatically deploys components that are sourced from Artifact Hub (utilizing Helm Charts). Support for OCI registries is expected in the near future.</p>
<details>
<summary><h4>Understanding CRDs and Why Deployment Order Matters</h4></summary>
<p><b>What is a CRD?</b></p>
<p>Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs) extend Kubernetes to support new resource types (e.g., <code>VirtualService</code>, <code>Gateway</code>). A CRD must be installed <b>before</b> any resource of that type is deployed, or you’ll encounter errors like <i>“no matches for kind…”</i>.</p>
<p><b>Why does Meshery only auto-deploy CRDs for ArtifactHub?</b></p>
<p>Helm Charts (used by ArtifactHub) are bundled with CRDs and operators, making it safe for Meshery to auto-deploy them via Helm Go client.</p>
<p>In contrast, Kubernetes YAML files may be minimal or incomplete. Meshery cannot assume what dependencies you intended. Therefore, Meshery avoids auto-deployment to prevent accidental conflicts or errors.</p>
<p><b>User Responsibility (for non-ArtifactHub components):</b></p>
<p>If you use Kubernetes YAML, ensure that all required CRDs and operators are included. Meshery will apply the YAML as-is using the Kubernetes Go client, but will <b>not auto-deploy</b> missing dependencies for you.</p>
</details>
<div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">Upcoming Features</div>
<p>Meshery is actively developing the ability to import custom models and components, expanding the platform's flexibility. Support for OCI registries is expected in the near future.</p><p><b>1. Custom Models and Components:</b> Import your own models for more flexibility.</p><p><b>2. OCI Registry Support:</b> In addition to ArtifactHub, OCI registries will be supported soon.</p>
</div>

        </div>

<script src="https://code.jquery.com/jquery-3.3.1.min.js"
    integrity="sha256-FgpCb/KJQlLNfOu91ta32o/NMZxltwRo8QtmkMRdAu8=" crossorigin="anonymous"></script>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Infrastructure Discovery</h1>
          
          <div class="alert alert-info" role="alert"><div class="h4 alert-heading" role="heading">MeshSync</div>
<p>Managed by the <a href='/concepts/architecture/operator'>Meshery Operator</a>, MeshSync is a custom Kubernetes controller that provides tiered discovery and continual synchronization with Meshery Server as to the state of the Kubernetes clusters and their workloads. Learn more about <a href='/concepts/architecture/meshsync'>MeshSync</a>.</p>
</div>
<p>MeshSync is your tool for efficient management and synchronization of Kubernetes clusters! This user guide will walk you through how to establish a connection with any element that Meshery is able to connect to and manage. Use the MeshSync page to register connections, view connection metadata, and perform connectivity tests, as weel as to manage credentials and environments.</p>
<h2 id="meshsync-discovery">
	MeshSync Discovery
</h2>
<p>MeshSync involves the discovery and registration of elements in your infrastructure. Follow these steps to seamlessly integrate and manage your connections:</p>
<ol>
<li><strong>Discovered</strong>: Fill out the registration form, specifying metrics to listen to for Prometheus.</li>
<li><strong>Register</strong>: Your object will now appear on the connection page.</li>
</ol>
<p>Tasks performed during registration:</p>
<ul>
<li>Enrich connections with more information about your infrastructure.</li>
<li>Offload fingerprinting process to MeshSync.</li>
<li>Connect with KubeAPI for connections management.</li>
<li>Handle curated list of connections (port, protocol, etc.).</li>
<li>Display Meshery Models icons/colors for every discovered object with connection definitions pointing to components.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="meshery-server-database-updates">
	Meshery Server Database Updates
</h3>
<p>Meshery Server writes updates from MeshSync to the server database:</p>
<p>Meshery uses the component&rsquo;s Group, Version, Kind to perform the initial tier of fingerprinting.</p>
<h3 id="meshsync-endpoint">
	MeshSync Endpoint
</h3>
<p>The Meshery Server endpoint performs a simple JOIN of GVKs to enrich responses with Component Metadata. Key points to note:</p>
<h2 id="connection-management">
	Connection Management
</h2>
<h3 id="during-connection-registration">
	During Connection Registration
</h3>
<p>Upon registration, the MeshSync object should have a status of &ldquo;REGISTERED.&rdquo; Follow these steps:</p>
<ol>
<li>Create a new entry in the Connections table with either &ldquo;REGISTERED&rdquo; or &ldquo;CONNECTED,&rdquo; based on the Meshery Server&rsquo;s ability to establish a connection.</li>
<li>Use the Registration Modal to assign the connection to an environment.</li>
<li>Confirm connection metadata details, including the assigned model and component.</li>
<li>Perform a connectivity test to determine the status: &ldquo;REGISTERED&rdquo; (administratively connected) or &ldquo;CONNECTED&rdquo; (both administratively and actually connected).</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="registration-modal">
	Registration Modal
</h3>
<p>The Registration Modal allows users to assign connections to environments, view connection metadata, and perform connectivity tests. Key features include:</p>
<ul>
<li>Connectivity test to determine registration status.</li>
<li>Identification of credentials to be used, with a selection based on CredentialDefinition for the ConnectionDefinition being registered.</li>
<li>Future options to offer generic CredentialDefinitions for various authentication methods.</li>
</ul>
<h3 id="credential-registration">
	Credential Registration
</h3>
<p>During credential registration, users can assign credentials to one or more connections and perform ad hoc connectivity tests. UI buttons include &ldquo;Test&rdquo; and &ldquo;Register.&rdquo;</p>
<h2 id="connection-configuration">
	Connection Configuration
</h2>
<p>The benefit of normalizing and extracting the status of a component as a direct property of the connection is to allow different systems to connect to the same component with different states. For example, multiple Meshery servers can connect to the same Kubernetes cluster, each having its own individual connection with a unique status.</p>
<p>Now that you are familiar with MeshSync and its powerful features, you are ready to streamline your Kubernetes cluster management.</p>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>

        <div class="td-content">
          
            <h1>Deploying Sample Applications</h1>
          
          <p>Meshery includes a few sample applications to help you explore cloud native infrastructure. Each is a collection of microservices for experimental purposes of learning about running workloads in Kubernetes clusters both on and off of cloud native infrastructure. When deploying a sample app onto your cloud native infrastructure, your sample application needs will need to be externaally exposed from the cluster, if you would like to access it externally. There are a myriad of ways to do this, specific to the infrastructure you are using.</p>
<p>A popular way of exposing your cluster is by using <a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/">Ingress</a>, an API object that defines rules which allow external access to services in a cluster.</p>
<ul>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/concepts/services-networking/ingress/#the-ingress-resource">Set up Ingress</a></li>
<li><a href="https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/access-application-cluster/ingress-minikube/">Set up Ingress on Minikube</a></li>
</ul>
<h2 id="deploy-a-sample-app-on-meshery">
	Deploy a sample app on Meshery
</h2>
<ol>
<li>
<p>Go to the management page of any infrastructure and install any of its stable versions.
<a href="./images/consul-install.png"><img alt="Consul-install" style="width:500px;height:auto;display:flex;padding-top:10px;" src="./images/consul-install.png" /></a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click (+) on <strong>Manage Sample Application Lifecycle</strong>. You will now be able to see a dropdown menu with the available sample applications.
<a href="./images/consul-sample-app.png"><img alt="ImageHub sample app" style="width:500px;height:auto;display:flex;padding-top:10px;" src="./images/consul-sample-app.png" /></a></p>
</li>
<li>
<p>Click on the sample application you want to deploy. This might take up to a minute. You will be notified when the sample application has been deployed.
<a href="./images/consul-imagehub-success.png"><img alt="ImageHub deployed" style="width:500px;height:auto;display:flex;padding-top:10px;" src="./images/consul-imagehub-success.png" /></a></p>
</li>
</ol>
<h3 id="bookinfo">
	BookInfo
</h3>
<p>Originally built by Istio, BookInfo is a sample application which on deployment displays information about a book, similar to a single catalog entry of an online book store. Displayed on the page is a description of the book, book details (ISBN, number of pages, and so on), and a few book reviews. The application comprises of four microservices:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>productpage</strong>: The productpage microservice calls the details and reviews microservices to populate the page.</li>
<li><strong>details</strong>: The details microservice contains book information.</li>
<li><strong>reviews</strong>: The reviews microservice contains book reviews. It also calls the ratings microservice.</li>
<li><strong>ratings</strong>: The ratings microservice contains book ranking information that accompanies a book review.</li>
</ul>
<p>Once BookInfo is deployed, you can use Meshery to apply custom configurations to control traffic, inject latency, perform context-based routing, and so on.</p>
<p><a href="./images/bookinfo.png"><img alt="BookInfo sample app" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/bookinfo.png" /></a></p>
<h3 id="emojivoto">
	<a href="https://github.com/BuoyantIO/emojivoto">Emojivoto</a>
</h3>
<p>Emojivoto is a microservice application, originally built by Linkerd that allows users to vote for their favorite emoji, and tracks votes received on a leaderboard. The application is composed of three microservices:</p>
<ul>
<li><strong>emojivoto-web</strong>: Web frontend and REST API</li>
<li><strong>emojivoto-emoji-svc</strong>: gRPC API for finding and listing emoji</li>
<li><strong>emojivoto-voting-svc</strong>: gRPC API for voting and leaderboard</li>
</ul>
<p><a href="./images/emojivoto.png"><img alt="Emojivoto" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/emojivoto.png" /></a></p>
<h3 id="imagehub">
</h3>
<p>Image Hub is a sample application for exploring WebAssembly modules used as Envoy filters. The application was originally written to run on Consul. However, it doesn&rsquo;t have any dependency on Consul and can be deployed on any infrastructure. These modules can be used to implement multi-tenancy or to implement per user rate limiting in your application’s endpoints, without messing with your application infrastructure.
<p><a href="./images/imagehub-on-consul.png"><img alt="Imagehub-on-Consul" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/imagehub-on-consul.png" /></a></p>
<h3 id="httpbin">
	<a href="https://httpbin.org">HTTPBin</a>
</h3>
<p>HttpBin is a simple HTTP request and response service that responds to many kinds of http/https requests including the standard http request methods (or verbs) used by REST.</p>
<p><a href="./images/httpbin.png"><img alt="httpbin" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/httpbin.png" /></a></p>
<h3 id="linkerd-books">
	<a href="https://github.com/BuoyantIO/booksapp">Linkerd Books</a>
</h3>
<p>Linkerd Books is a sample Ruby based application. It is designed to demonstrate the various value propositions, including debugging, observability, and monitoring of your infrastructure. It can be used to scope out your mesh&rsquo;s efficiency and for debugging.</p>
<p><a href="./images/linkerd-books.png"><img alt="Linkerd Books" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/linkerd-books.png" /></a></p>
<h3 id="online-boutique">
	<a href="https://github.com/GoogleCloudPlatform/microservices-demo">Online Boutique</a>
</h3>
<p>Online Boutique is a sample cloud-native application, originally built by Google. It comprises of 10 microservices and can be used to showcase and work with Kubernetes, Istio, gRPC and OpenCensus. On deployment, it runs a web-based e-commerce demo application, an example of which can be seen below:</p>
<p><a href="./images/online-boutique.png"><img alt="Online Boutique" style="width:500px;height:auto;" src="./images/online-boutique.png" /></a></p>

        </div>

<script>
    $(document).ready(function () {

        var toc = $('#TOC');

        
        
        
        
        var hasH1 = $('.td-content h1').length > 0;
        var topSelector = hasH1 ? 'h1' : 'h2';
        var subSelector = hasH1 ? 'h2, h3' : 'h3';

        sections = $('.td-content ' + topSelector);

        $.each(sections, function (idx, v) {
            section = $(v);
            var div_id = $(section).attr('id');
            if (!section.hasClass('noTOC')) {
                var div_text = section.text().split('¶')[0];
                var parent = $("#" + div_id)
                var content = '<li id="link_' + div_id + '" class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + div_id + '" title="' + div_text + '">' + div_text + '</a></li>';
                $(document).find(toc).append(content);
            }

            
            var children = $('<nav class="md-nav"><ul class="md-nav__list"></nav></ul>')
            var contenders = $("#" + div_id).nextUntil(topSelector);
            $.each(contenders, function (idx, contender) {
                if (!$(contender).hasClass("noTOC") && $(contender).is(subSelector)) {
                    var contender_id = $(contender).attr('id');
                    var contender_text = $(contender).text().split('¶')[0];
                    var content = '<li class="md-nav__item"><a class="md-nav__link" href="#' + contender_id + '" title="' + contender_text + '">' + contender_text + '</a></li>';
                    children.append(content);
                }
            })
            $("#link_" + div_id).append(children);
        });
        
        $('.md-nav__link').first().addClass('selected');

        $(window).scroll(function (e) {
            
            let windowTop = $(this).scrollTop();
            
            $('.md-nav__link').each(function (event) {
                if (windowTop >= $($(this).attr('href')).offset().top - 100) {
                    
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
                if ($(window).scrollTop() + $(window).height() > $(document).height() - 10) {
                    $('.selected').removeClass('selected');
                    $(this).addClass('selected');
                }
            });
        })
    });
</script>
